lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your petrol caddy request needs a safety check — I'll review the brief before building.

Declined — I can't build this as asked.

**What you asked for:** a caddy that holds two jerry cans of petrol upright in the boot of a car.

**Why I can't build it:**
- The parts are 3D-printed plastic and the configurator checks fit only. It knows nothing about materials, strength, load ratings, fuel or heat resistance.
- Holding petrol / fuel is on the unsafe list: a build that would hold fuel or anything burning or hot must be declined or compromised. Petrol in a printed plastic caddy, loose in a car boot, risks leaks, fumes, fire/explosion, and crash loads the system cannot rate or restrain for.
- I can't verify it would restrain the cans in a moving car.

**What I could build instead:**
A caddy for cold, non-flammable tools or for empty, clean containers for workshop storage — e.g. a two-bay carrier with bins/handles for the bench — but not for petrol and not for use in a car boot.

No parts were added for this purpose.
Switching to the safe alternative — a workshop tool caddy. I'll start gathering parts.
